reason: E3 directly supports the first three premises by showing higher chemisorbed oxygen, lower activation energy, and superior CO oxidation for Pd1@HEFO vs. Pd@CeO2. E1 shows that increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity and long-term stability, partially supporting the last two premises, but it does not involve Pd or fluorite supports. E2 is a general background on pollution and catalytic oxidation and provides no specific support for any premise.
premises: Pd single atoms on high-entropy fluorite oxide (HEFO) create more oxygen vacancies than Pd on CeO2
These oxygen vacancies enhance O2 activation and lattice oxygen reducibility near Pd
Enhanced oxygen activation enables a Mars–van Krevelen mechanism that lowers CO oxidation onset temperature
The single-atom Pd/HEFO catalyst resists sintering and deactivation under hydrothermal conditions
High-entropy oxide supports improve long-term stability compared to conventional supports
